name: Plugin Starter
description: Read this if you want to build a plugin for the editor. Adds one menu entry plus a small dock panel so you can see every PluginAPI v2 surface in action.
long_description:
What you get

One menu entry under Marketplace → Plugin Starter: Quickstart. Click it and the editor opens a tab with a self-contained guide to authoring a plugin: folder layout, manifest fields, the register(api) entry point, the full PluginAPI v2 surface, and how to publish to the marketplace via Nostr.

You also get a side panel labelled Plugin Starter Panel. It shows a click counter, a ticking timer, and a button, so you can see what an interactive plugin dock widget looks like and read the source that builds it.

How to use this as a template

  1. Copy bundled_plugins/hello_world/ to your user plugins folder (~/.config/my-editor/plugins/ on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/my-editor/plugins/ on macOS, %APPDATA%/my-editor/plugins/ on Windows).
  2. Rename the folder to your plugin's id.
  3. Edit manifest.json and __init__.py to your taste. The source is heavily commented as a learning example.
  4. Restart the editor; your plugin appears in the Marketplace menu and (if you keep the dock widget code) on the right side of the editor window.

What plugins can do today (PluginAPI v2)

  • add_menu_action(menu, label, callback): add a clickable entry to the menu bar.
  • add_dock_widget(title, widget_factory, area="right"): attach a side panel. Requires the dock_widget capability.
  • register_unload(callback): register a teardown function for timers and threads so the plugin can be disabled cleanly.
  • get_current_text() / set_current_text(text): read or rewrite the active tab.
  • open_tab(title, content): open a new tab populated with text.
  • get_setting(key, default) / set_setting(key, value): persist data scoped to your plugin (other plugins cannot see it).
  • publish_event(template): sign and publish a Nostr event under the user's connected profile. Each kind you publish MUST be declared in manifest.json's declared_kinds.
  • register_payment_provider(provider): offer to pay invoices for paid plugin installs.

Safety boundaries

Plugins run with full Python access; the editor sandboxes capability surfaces, not the process. Don't import from main_window, nostr, or editor: the api argument is the entire supported surface. The following Nostr kinds cannot be published via publish_event even when declared, because they control the user's identity, trust graph, or relay routing: 0 (kind:0 metadata), 3 (NIP-02 follows), 5 (NIP-09 deletions), 10000 (NIP-51 mutes), 10002 (NIP-65 relay list), 24133 (NIP-46 bunker RPC).

Distribution

Plugins surface in this marketplace via a kind:30700 Nostr listing event published by the plugin author. Once you have one, anyone running this editor can find your plugin without trusting a central registry.

Going deeper

The full PluginAPI reference and the manifest schema live in the project's PLUGIN_DEVELOPMENT.md. The bundled __init__.py source is itself the second half of the tutorial: open it once you've read the in-editor quickstart.
